@about: Help for every command (app/CommandHelp.hpp): one record per command id. Translations by id in commands.<language>.json.

commands.title: New document
commands.summary: Starts a new, empty OPAD design.
commands.details: The current document is closed first; if it has unsaved changes you are asked whether to save them. The new design has no file until you save it.

commands.title: Open
commands.summary: Opens an OPAD document, a CAD model, a mesh or a 2D drawing.
commands.details: OPAD documents open for editing. STEP, IGES, STL, 3MF, OBJ, DXF, DWG, SVG and the other formats open read-only in viewer mode, which is fast; Save turns them into editable OPAD documents.

commands.title: Clone repository
commands.summary: Copies a git repository to this computer and opens its OPAD documents.
commands.details: Type the address, the folder it goes into and its name, then Clone. The copy is set up for OPAD's merge and difference tools, and its .opad documents are offered to open.
commands.requires: git must be installed; Locate git… points OPAD to it.

commands.title: Compare versions
commands.summary: Shows two versions of the document in one view: what was added, removed, changed or moved.
commands.details: Pick A and B in the Compare panel: this session, the saved file, git commits, recovery snapshots or another file. The view draws B tinted by change with ghosts of A, the panel lists the changes and Next change ({key:vcs.nextChange}) steps through them; Done or Esc ends it.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Show unsaved changes
commands.summary: Compares the saved file with this session: what changed since the last save.
commands.details: It opens Compare with the saved file as A and this session as B. The unsaved-changes question offers it too, as Review changes.
commands.requires: Only for a saved OPAD document with unsaved changes.

commands.title: Version control
commands.summary: Opens the Version control panel: the branch and its remote, the document's state, its history and the branches.
commands.details: Commit, push, pull and switch branches from there; the git chip beside the path opens it too. A document that is not in a repository yet is offered one.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Commit
commands.summary: Records the document (saved first) and the files you tick in git, with a message.
commands.details: The message is suggested from what changed since the last commit, and the author is asked for once. You can amend the last commit while it is not pushed, and push right after.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Push
commands.summary: Sends your commits to the remote repository.
commands.details: The first push sets up the remote branch, adding a remote when there is none, and warns about big files. Commit first: a branch with no commits has nothing to push.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Pull
commands.summary: Fetches the remote's commits and shows what they change in the document before merging them.
commands.details: Conflicts and changes made on both sides are listed, with Preview in Compare and Merge. The branch must follow a remote branch; Push sets that up.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Fetch
commands.summary: Downloads the remote's new commits without changing your files.
commands.details: The git chip then shows how far ahead of or behind the remote your branch is. Fetch in the background does it every 10 minutes, quietly.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: New branch
commands.summary: Starts a branch at the current commit to try a variant of the design.
commands.details: Name it in the dialog; History can also start a branch from an older commit. Commit first: a branch starts at a commit.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: History
commands.summary: Lists the commits of the document in the Version control panel.
commands.details: Compare a commit with this session or with the commit before, open it read-only, restore it as new changes, or start a branch from it. Show in version history on a timeline marker narrows the list to the commits that touched that step.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Branches
commands.summary: Lists the branches: switch to one, create, delete or merge one into the current branch.
commands.details: Unsaved and uncommitted changes are asked about before a switch, and a merge shows what it brings in first. Abort merge is there while a merge stopped on conflicts.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Pack the repository
commands.summary: Packs the repository's loose objects so it takes less space.
commands.details: It runs git's maintenance on a worker and says what it saved. After a commit it is offered when many loose objects have piled up.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Resolve conflicts
commands.summary: Settles a merge that stopped on the document, change by change.
commands.details: What both sides changed is listed: choose mine or theirs for each, or keep a whole side. The file is then written and added, Regenerate is offered, and you commit the merge.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Fetch in the background
commands.summary: Fetches from the remote every 10 minutes, quietly.
commands.details: It never asks for a sign-in; turn it off on a metered or slow connection. Fetch does it once by hand.

commands.title: Next change
commands.summary: Goes to the next change in Compare.
commands.details: Its row in the panel is selected and its bodies are fitted in the view. Previous change ({key:vcs.previousChange}) goes back.
commands.requires: Only while Compare is open.

commands.title: Previous change
commands.summary: Goes to the previous change in Compare.
commands.details: Its row in the panel is selected and its bodies are fitted in the view. Next change ({key:vcs.nextChange}) goes forward.
commands.requires: Only while Compare is open.

commands.title: Import
commands.summary: Adds a CAD model, mesh or drawing file to this design.
commands.details: The file's parts join the open document as new bodies, under the selected component if you choose to. A 2D drawing asks where it goes: onto a selected planar face, or on a plane you pick and place. A KiCad board first asks what to build.
commands.requires: A file in viewer mode asks you to save it as an OPAD document first.

commands.title: Save as OPAD document
commands.summary: Saves the file open in viewer mode as an editable OPAD document.
commands.details: The shapes already on screen are kept, so nothing is read again. The file you opened is left as it is; from then on you edit the new .opad document.
commands.requires: Only for a file open in viewer mode (STEP, STL, DXF and the other formats).

commands.title: Save
commands.summary: Saves the document; a file in viewer mode becomes an editable OPAD document.
commands.details: A document that has never been saved asks for a file name. Saving appends the new steps to the .opad file, which stays friendly to git and to merges.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Save As
commands.summary: Saves the document under a new file name.
commands.details: The document continues under the new name; the old file stays as it was last saved. Use it to start a variant of a design.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Save as template
commands.summary: Keeps a copy of the document among the templates that New from template offers.
commands.details: The copy goes into the templates folder under the name you give, with an identity of its own. A document made from it starts as an untitled copy, so the template itself never changes.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first (a file in viewer mode cannot be a template until it is saved as OPAD).

commands.title: Export
commands.summary: Writes the selection or the whole design to STEP, STL, OBJ, GLB, DXF, SVG, DWG, PDF or PNG.
commands.details: Choose the format and what to include in the dialog, then where the file goes. Mesh formats are tessellated from the exact shapes; the 2D formats write drawings and sketches, or a 2D view of solids with hidden lines.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Export bill of materials
commands.summary: Writes a parts list of the selection or the whole design to a CSV file.
commands.details: Choose the list (parts only, top level or indented), of the whole document or the selected component, whether masses are listed and in which unit, and the separator; the preview shows the table. Export CSV then asks where the file goes.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Document properties
commands.summary: Edits what every drawing's title block says: title, number, revision, status, owner, project and who designed, checked and approved it.
commands.details: The values are stored in the document as one step, and a sheet can still say otherwise. Add properties of your own and use them in a title block field as =doc:name.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; a viewed file is saved as OPAD first.

commands.title: Save screenshot
commands.summary: Saves an image of the 3D view.
commands.details: A dialog asks where to save the PNG. The image is the 3D view as it is now, at its size on screen; panels and chips are left out.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Open file location
commands.summary: Shows the open document's file in the system's file manager.
commands.details: For a file open in viewer mode it is the viewed file. The status bar's path and the browser's document row offer it too.
commands.requires: The document must have a file: save it first.

commands.title: Copy path
commands.summary: Copies the full path of the open document's file to the clipboard.
commands.details: For a file open in viewer mode it is the viewed file. The status bar's path menu also has Copy relative path.
commands.requires: The document must have a file: save it first.

commands.title: Close document
commands.summary: Closes the document and returns to the start screen.
commands.details: If there are unsaved changes you are asked whether to save them. Recent files stay on the start screen.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Quit
commands.summary: Closes OPAD.
commands.details: You are asked about unsaved changes first. Window layout and settings are kept for the next start.

commands.title: Use the ODA File Converter for DWG
commands.summary: Reads and writes DWG through an installed ODA File Converter instead of LibreDWG.
commands.details: The ODA File Converter is third-party software whose licence lets non-members use it for non-commercial purposes only, so turning this on first shows its terms. Off, OPAD converts DWG with LibreDWG's dwg2dxf and dxf2dwg, beside OPAD or on PATH. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Fit
commands.summary: Zooms to the selection; with nothing selected, to the active component or to everything.
commands.details: The camera keeps its direction and only moves and zooms. While a sketch is open it fits the sketch.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Fit all
commands.summary: Zooms so the whole model fits the view.
commands.details: Unlike Fit, the selection is ignored. While a sketch is open it fits the sketch.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Home
commands.summary: Returns to the home camera: an isometric view with everything in sight.
commands.details: Use it when you lose your way after orbiting. The view cube's house button does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Align view to plane
commands.summary: Turns the camera to look straight at the sketch plane or at a plane you pick.
commands.details: While sketching it aligns to the sketch at once. Otherwise pick a planar face or an origin plane, and the camera turns square to it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Turn 90° left
commands.summary: Turns the view 90 degrees to the left about the screen's axis.
commands.details: The model is not moved, only the camera. Use it to stand a drawing or a face upright.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Turn 90° right
commands.summary: Turns the view 90 degrees to the right about the screen's axis.
commands.details: The model is not moved, only the camera. Use it to stand a drawing or a face upright.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Top view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from above, along -Z.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Front view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the front, along +Y.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Right view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the right, along -X.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Isometric view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from a corner, at equal angles to the three axes.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Bottom view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from below, along +Z.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Back view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the back, along -Y.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Left view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the left, along +X.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Next region
commands.summary: Moves the keyboard to the next part of the window: ribbon, browser, view, timeline, then each open panel.
commands.details: The part reached is ringed, and its controls take the keys: arrows in the ribbon's tabs, the browser and the timeline, Tab in a panel. After the last panel it starts again at the ribbon; a click anywhere takes the ring away.

commands.title: Previous region
commands.summary: Moves the keyboard back to the part of the window before this one.
commands.details: The same round as Next region, the other way: from a panel back to the timeline, the view, the browser and the ribbon. It works from a floating panel too.

commands.title: 2D mode
commands.summary: Locks the view to a plane for drawings: pan and zoom only.
commands.details: Orbiting is off and the grid lies in the viewed plane, following the view so it never ends. Opening a DXF, DWG or SVG for viewing turns it on by itself; the 2D mode chip or this command turns it off.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Layers
commands.summary: Opens the Layers manager of the document's 2D drawings.
commands.details: One row per layer: On, Freeze, Lock, Colour, Linetype, Lineweight and Plot change with a click, each one step to undo, in viewer mode too. Isolate layers, walk through them one at a time, and save layer states with a view.
commands.requires: Only for a document with 2D drawings (DXF, DWG or SVG).

commands.title: Layer walk
commands.summary: Shows the drawings one layer at a time.
commands.details: The walk starts at the current layer of the Layers manager, and its bar steps to the next or the previous layer, off and frozen ones included. Run it again, or close the panel, to see every layer again.
commands.requires: Only for a document with 2D drawings (DXF, DWG or SVG).

commands.title: Isolate layer
commands.summary: Shows only the selected layers.
commands.details: Select the layers in the Layers manager first. Exit isolate ({key:view.unisolate}) brings the others back.
commands.requires: Select one or more layers first.

commands.title: Object snap
commands.summary: Snaps picked points to the ends, middles, centres, intersections and other points of drawing objects.
commands.details: It applies while measuring and picking points; which kinds it takes are the sketch's snap settings. Its switch is in the status bar beside the other snapping switches.

commands.title: Plot
commands.summary: Plots the 2D drawings to a PDF file or a printer.
commands.details: Choose the area (the drawings' extents, what the view shows, or a window picked in the view), the paper and its orientation, fit or a 1:N scale, monochrome and lineweights. A preview shows the page as it will come out.
commands.requires: Only for a document with 2D drawings.

commands.title: Orthographic
commands.summary: Switches between orthographic and perspective projection.
commands.details: Orthographic keeps parallel edges parallel, which suits measuring and drawings. Perspective looks more natural for presenting a model.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Shaded
commands.summary: Draws bodies shaded, without edge lines.
commands.details: The cleanest look for presenting a design. Picking works as in the other styles.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Shaded + edges
commands.summary: Draws shaded bodies with their edges.
commands.details: The default style: faces and their boundaries are both easy to read. Edges are drawn in the theme's edge colour.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Wireframe
commands.summary: Draws edges only; hidden edges show through.
commands.details: Useful to see inner features and to pick edges behind faces. Faces are not drawn, but clicks still find them.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Grid
commands.summary: Shows or hides the ground grid.
commands.details: In 3D the grid is a patch under the model, spaced to the model's size; in 2D mode and in sketches it follows the view and its spacing follows the zoom. A fixed spacing set in Grid settings is used everywhere.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Grid settings
commands.summary: Sets the grid spacing, automatic or fixed, and its minimum extent.
commands.details: Automatic spacing follows the zoom in sketches and 2D mode and the model's size in 3D; a fixed spacing is what grid snapping jumps to. The grid is turned on while you change it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Select through objects
commands.summary: Lets a selection window also pick what is completely hidden behind other bodies, and a click in the Edges or Vertices filter reach edges and points behind faces.
commands.details: Off, a window picks whatever shows inside it, even partly. On, a window drag selects every body inside it, front or back.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Isolate
commands.summary: Shows only the selection until you exit isolation.
commands.details: Everything else is hidden from view, not from the document. Exit isolate ({key:view.unisolate}) brings it back.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Exit isolate
commands.summary: Brings back everything isolation hid.
commands.details: The camera stays where it is. Visibility you set yourself is kept.
commands.requires: Nothing is isolated.

commands.title: Save view
commands.summary: Saves the current camera as a named view.
commands.details: Named views are stored in the document and listed under View > Named views. Pick one to return to that camera. A file open in viewer mode asks to become an OPAD document first.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Dark theme
commands.summary: Switches between the dark and the light theme.
commands.details: Every panel, icon and the 3D view follow the theme. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Extensions
commands.summary: Draws dashed extensions of hovered edges; the cursor snaps onto them and to where two cross.
commands.details: Rest on the end of a line, then move along its direction to follow the dashed line. Works in sketches and while measuring or picking points, drawings included.

commands.title: Tracking
commands.summary: Shows alignment lines through points you hover, along X, Y and Z.
commands.details: Rest on a point to acquire it, then move away: a dashed line appears when the cursor lines up with it. Hold Shift to lock onto the line; a tap keeps it locked until Esc. With several guides or snaps in reach, a tap shows the next.

commands.title: Grid snapping
commands.summary: Makes placed points jump to grid intersections.
commands.details: Applies to points you click in sketches, and when placing a drawing or a sketch's origin. Hold Alt to place a point off the grid. Set a fixed spacing in Grid settings for predictable steps.

commands.title: Ortho
commands.summary: Keeps each new line of a sketch horizontal or vertical.
commands.details: The next point lines up with the last one along whichever axis is nearer the cursor. Snaps to points and curves still win; with automatic constraints on, the line gets its horizontal or vertical constraint. Right-click the switch for its settings.

commands.title: Polar
commands.summary: Turns a sketch line's direction in fixed angle steps.
commands.details: Near a multiple of the angle step the line snaps to it. Right-click the switch to choose the step: 5, 10, 15, 22.5, 30, 45 or 90 degrees.

commands.title: View cube edges and corners turn the view
commands.summary: Lets a click on the view cube's edges and corners turn the view, besides its faces.
commands.details: On, an edge shows the view between its two faces and a corner the isometric view from its side. Off, only the six faces react, which are easier to hit on a small cube. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Browser
commands.summary: Shows or hides the browser: the document's components, bodies, sketches and drawings.
commands.details: Click a row to select it, use the eye to hide it, and drag rows onto a component to move them. Filter objects ({key:edit.filter}) filters it by name.

commands.title: Annotations
commands.summary: Lists notes, hand drawings and pinned measurements.
commands.details: Filter by author, type and status; click a card to show its target. Resolved notes stay in the history.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; a file in viewer mode has no annotations.

commands.title: Section panel
commands.summary: Opens the section panel: axis, offset, caps and named sections.
commands.details: Here you choose the cutting axis or a face, type an exact offset and save sections by name. Dragging the plane's edge in the view does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Timeline
commands.summary: Shows or hides the timeline: every step of the document's history.
commands.details: Each marker is one operation; hover it for who did what and when. Double-click a feature or sketch to edit it.

commands.title: Names on the timeline
commands.summary: Writes each step's name beside its icon on the timeline.
commands.details: Off, the markers show their icons only and the names are in their tooltips. The choice is kept for the next session.

commands.title: Design history only
commands.summary: Keeps the timeline to the steps that make and place geometry.
commands.details: Imports, sketches, features and moves stay; renames, colours, views and sections are left off the timeline, though they stay in the document. The browser's history list follows it.

commands.title: Roll forward to the end
commands.summary: Shows the model with every step again after the timeline was rolled back.
commands.details: Dragging the timeline's marker back shows the model as it was before a step, and a chip over the view says so. This command, or a click on the chip, rolls forward to the end.
commands.requires: Only while the timeline is rolled back.

commands.title: History list in the browser
commands.summary: Lists the timeline's steps in a History folder in the browser.
commands.details: They are listed top to bottom, with the roll-back marker among them. The choice is kept for the next session.

commands.title: Reset layout
commands.summary: Puts the panels and docks back where they started.
commands.details: Floating tool panels return to their default place and size. Use it when a panel got lost off screen.

commands.title: Review workspace
commands.summary: Switches the ribbon to Review: look, measure, annotate.
commands.details: Review's tools look, measure and annotate; apart from Import they leave geometry and structure alone. The document and its timeline stay the same; only the ribbon's tabs change. Finish an open sketch first.

commands.title: Design workspace
commands.summary: Switches the ribbon to Design: sketches, features, parameters and the assembly.
commands.details: Design is where parts are modelled and arranged. The selection filter returns to bodies when you switch.

commands.title: Drawings workspace
commands.summary: Switches to the Drawings workspace: sheets with views, a frame and a title block in the 3D view's place.
commands.details: The sheet shown replaces the 3D view while this workspace is on, and the browser's Drawings folder lists the drawings and their sheets. The document and its timeline stay the same; only the ribbon's tabs and the page change.

commands.title: New drawing
commands.summary: Starts a technical drawing of the model: a sheet with a frame, a title block and standard views.
commands.details: Choose the template and paper, the projection (first or third angle), the scale, the views and their style, of the whole model or the selection; the title block's first fields can be filled in here. The views are laid out on a worker and the Drawings workspace opens on the new sheet.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; a viewed file is saved as OPAD first.

commands.title: New sheet
commands.summary: Adds another sheet to the drawing shown, with its paper, template and scale.
commands.details: The new sheet starts empty: place views on it with Base view. The browser lists the sheets under their drawing in the Drawings folder.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Sheet properties
commands.summary: Edits the sheet shown: its name, paper, projection, scale and the title block values it sets itself.
commands.details: The change is one step. Values it leaves empty come from Document properties.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Template from DXF or DWG
commands.summary: Takes the frame and title block of the sheet shown from a DXF or DWG file, such as a company template.
commands.details: The file is read on a worker; its frame replaces the sheet's template and its paper size is taken too. The change is one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view
commands.summary: Places a front view of the model on the sheet: a frame follows the pointer and a click places it.
commands.details: The other orientations (from the top, right, left, back and below) are on the button's menu. The frame snaps to the other views' centres, and a view dragged later takes the views projected from it along.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the top
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the top on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the right
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the right on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the left
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the left on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the back
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the back on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from below
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from below on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Projected view
commands.summary: Adds a view projected from the selected one, on the side the pointer is on.
commands.details: Select one view on the sheet, run it and move to its right, left, top or bottom, or a corner: the new view lines up with it and a click places it. A projected view keeps to its parent's line when either is dragged.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Isometric view
commands.summary: Places an isometric view of the model on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame follows the pointer and a click places it. It is a pictorial view, not projected from the others.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Hidden lines
commands.summary: Shows or hides dashed hidden lines in the selected views, or in every view of the sheet.
commands.details: It changes the views' style as one step. With no view selected it applies to the whole sheet.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Tangent edges
commands.summary: Draws the edges where faces meet smoothly as thin lines, or leaves them out.
commands.details: It changes the selected views' style, or every view's when none is selected, as one step. A view's right-click menu also draws them as ordinary edges.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Update views
commands.summary: Projects the sheet's views again from the model as it is now.
commands.details: The views are projected on a worker; until each is ready its old drawing stays, marked Updating. Nothing in the document changes.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Fit sheet
commands.summary: Zooms the sheet so all of it shows.
commands.details: It changes only how the sheet is shown, never the drawing. The wheel zooms about the pointer and a middle drag pans.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Export sheet
commands.summary: Writes the sheet shown to PDF, SVG, DXF, DWG or PNG.
commands.details: Choose the file and its type; it is written on a worker. A drawing with several sheets goes into one PDF from its row in the browser's Drawings folder.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Navigation: Fusion-style
commands.summary: Uses Fusion-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse, not the keyboard shortcuts. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Navigation: SOLIDWORKS-style
commands.summary: Uses SOLIDWORKS-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse, not the keyboard shortcuts. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Navigation: Onshape-style
commands.summary: Uses Onshape-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse, not the keyboard shortcuts. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Navigation: Blender-style
commands.summary: Uses Blender-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse, not the keyboard shortcuts. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Bodies
commands.summary: Makes a click pick whole bodies.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. The default for Design; Review measures pick what the tool needs.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Faces
commands.summary: Makes a click pick faces of bodies.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. Faces are what you measure, sketch on and press-pull.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Edges
commands.summary: Makes a click pick edges, and the lines and curves of drawings.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. Edges are what fillets and chamfers work on.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Vertices
commands.summary: Makes a click pick vertices, the corner points of bodies.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. Vertices are handy as exact points for measuring.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Distance
commands.summary: Measures the shortest distance between two picks.
commands.details: Pick two faces, edges, vertices or bodies; the result shows the distance and its X, Y and Z parts. A dashed preview line follows the cursor after the first pick, and Pin ({key:inspect.pin}) keeps the result in the document.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Angle
commands.summary: Measures the angle between two faces or edges.
commands.details: Pick the first face or edge, then the second. The result shows the angle and its supplement.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Radius
commands.summary: Measures the radius and diameter of a circular edge or a cylindrical face.
commands.details: Pick one round face, or a circular edge with the Edges filter. The result shows R and Ø; Pin ({key:inspect.pin}) keeps it in the document.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Bounding box
commands.summary: Draws the world-aligned box around the picks and reports its size.
commands.details: Pick one or more bodies, faces or edges. The box is measured tightly on a worker thread, so large parts do not freeze the view.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Area
commands.summary: Measures the area and perimeter enclosed by picked faces, edges or drawing objects, or by picked points.
commands.details: Each pick adds to the boundary: faces give their exact area, edges and objects the loops they close (a loop inside another is a hole), three points or more the polygon through them. One object that encloses nothing alone grows into the smallest area around the clicked part; while the picks enclose nothing the panel says what is still open. Pin ({key:inspect.pin}) keeps the result in the document.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Interference
commands.summary: Finds bodies that overlap or nearly touch and lists each pair.
commands.details: Checks the selected bodies, or all solids when nothing is selected. Click a row to highlight that overlap in the view.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Print check
commands.summary: Checks a part for 3D printing: overhangs, build-plate contact and thin walls.
commands.details: Works on solids and on meshes such as STL and 3MF. Each finding is a region; click it to highlight it on the part.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Pin
commands.summary: Keeps the current measurement in the document as an annotation.
commands.details: A pinned measurement stays visible, appears in the Annotations panel and is part of the history. Remove it there when it is no longer needed.
commands.requires: Measure something first with Distance, Angle, Radius or Bounding box.

commands.title: Clear measurement
commands.summary: Steps back one level: closes a popup or panel, cancels a pick, leaves a tool or clears the measurement.
commands.details: Esc always undoes the most recent thing first. Press it again to keep stepping back until nothing is left.

commands.title: Properties
commands.summary: Shows the properties of the selection: name, id, volume, area and size.
commands.details: Names and ids show at once; volume, area and the exact box are measured in the background and fill in. Pin the panel to make it follow the selection.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Part properties
commands.summary: Gives the selected bodies or components a part number, description, material, density or mass, vendor and notes.
commands.details: The fields feed the bill of materials and the drawings' title blocks, and a material from the library gives the mass from the volume. Several objects are edited at once, as one step, and Properties shows the result in its Part section.
commands.requires: Select bodies or components first.

commands.title: Select similar
commands.summary: Selects every face or edge like the picked one: the same hole, fillet radius or direction; for a body picked whole, a rule.
commands.details: Pick a face or an edge of a solid, then Select similar: the matches are found on a worker and selected at once; run it again for the next rule. On a body picked whole it starts with the top perimeter, then the bottom perimeter, edges along X, Y or Z, circular edges, upward faces, holes, fillets and chamfers. Useful to pick every hole at once for a fillet.
commands.requires: Pick a face or an edge of a solid, or a body, first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Section
commands.summary: Cuts the view with a plane to look inside; drag the plane's edge to move it.
commands.details: Only the view is cut, never the model. Cut faces get caps so solids read as solid, and the Section panel holds exact offsets and named sections.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Flip section
commands.summary: Shows the other side of the section.
commands.details: The cutting plane stays where it is; the kept half swaps. Turn Section on first.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Note
commands.summary: Pins a text note to a body, face, edge or point.
commands.details: Click the target (the selection filter decides whether that is a body, face, edge or point), type the note and save it with {fixed:ctrlEnter}. Notes keep their author and time, and live in the document's history.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document, and finish the sketch first.

commands.title: Hand drawing
commands.summary: Draws freehand strokes on the model.
commands.details: Pick a target, then drag to draw; each stroke lies on a plane facing the camera, so it stays in place when you orbit. Save keeps the drawing as one annotation.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document, and finish the sketch first.

commands.title: Resolve note
commands.summary: Marks the selected note as resolved.
commands.details: A resolved note leaves the view and is dimmed in the Annotations panel, where Restore brings it back; it stays in the history, so the discussion is never lost. Filter the panel by status to hide them.
commands.requires: Select a note in the Annotations panel first.

commands.title: Show notes
commands.summary: Shows or hides note cards in the 3D view.
commands.details: Hiding them only declutters the view. The notes stay in the document and in the Annotations panel.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Undo
commands.summary: Undoes the last change.
commands.details: In a sketch it undoes the last sketch edit; in the note editor the last stroke. Undo history keeps the last 50 steps by default.
commands.requires: Nothing to undo.

commands.title: Redo
commands.summary: Redoes the change you just undid.
commands.details: Redo is available until you make a new change. In a sketch it redoes sketch edits.
commands.requires: Nothing to redo.

commands.title: Cut
commands.summary: Copies the selection and then deletes it, as Delete does.
commands.details: Paste ({key:edit.paste}) puts it back, here or in another OPAD window; in a sketch it cuts the selected curves. Undo brings the originals back.

commands.title: Copy
commands.summary: Copies the selected bodies and components, or in a sketch the selected curves with the constraints among them.
commands.details: Paste ({key:edit.paste}) then makes copies, also in another OPAD window. With nothing selected, the current timeline marker's operation id is copied instead.

commands.title: Paste
commands.summary: Places what was copied: bodies as new bodies, sketch curves in the open sketch.
commands.details: In the document they came from, the copies start beside the originals in a Move / copy panel, and Enter makes them; from another document they are imported as they were. In a sketch the curves follow the pointer by their base point until a click places them.

commands.title: Paste as linked instances
commands.summary: Puts the copied parts in again as instances of the same stored bodies.
commands.details: The instances use the bodies the originals use rather than copies of them, and the Linked instances panel lists them. It is one undo step.

commands.title: Repeat
commands.summary: Runs the last tool, feature, check or edit again.
commands.details: The menu entry names the command it repeats, and it is the first entry of the view's context menu. Enter in the view repeats it too while nothing runs, except Delete, Restore, Hide and Show all, which repeat only from here. View navigation, file open and save, panel toggles and plain selection commands are not repeated; Import, Export, Screenshot, Isolate, Save view and Select similar are.

commands.title: Select all
commands.summary: Selects every body on screen, or every curve of the sketch being edited.
commands.details: Hidden bodies and those outside an isolation stay out. In a face, edge or vertex filter the view goes back to bodies first; while a tool or a feature input is picking, nothing changes.

commands.title: Invert selection
commands.summary: Selects the bodies on screen that are not selected, and lets go of those that are.
commands.details: In a sketch it swaps the selected and unselected curves. Use it to pick everything but a few parts: select those, then invert.

commands.title: Rename
commands.summary: Renames the selection; several objects are numbered where {n} stands.
commands.details: One object is renamed in place in the browser. For several, type a name such as Leg {n} and they become Leg 1, Leg 2 and so on, in selection order.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Hide
commands.summary: Hides the selection.
commands.details: Hidden objects stay in the document; the browser's eye shows them again. Unhide all ({key:edit.showall}) brings back everything.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Unhide all
commands.summary: Shows everything that is hidden.
commands.details: Bodies, components and sketches you hid become visible again. Isolation is separate: leave it with Exit isolate.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Filter objects
commands.summary: Opens the browser and puts the cursor in its name filter.
commands.details: Type part of a name to narrow the browser to matching rows. Clear the field to see everything again.

commands.title: Select parent
commands.summary: Selects the component that contains the selection.
commands.details: Press it again to climb further up the assembly. Useful after clicking a single body deep inside an imported model.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Select less
commands.summary: Steps the selection back down what Select parent climbed.
commands.details: From a feature's faces back to the faces picked first, from a component to its body. Select parent ({key:edit.selectparent}) climbs up again.

commands.title: Related selections
commands.summary: Lists what the picked faces or edges belong to, with what can be done to it.
commands.details: The feature that made them, a hole, a fillet chain or a loop: pick one to select it, or delete, edit or suppress it, or find it in the timeline. The smart chip's ▾ opens the same list.

commands.title: Suggest related selections
commands.summary: Shows a chip beside picked faces or edges naming what they belong to.
commands.details: A click on the chip, or Select parent ({key:edit.selectparent}), selects that whole feature or detail, and on such a selection the chip carries its actions. Off, the chip comes only with Select parent, Related selections or Delete.

commands.title: Delete
commands.summary: Removes the selection; the history keeps it restorable.
commands.details: In a design the bodies leave through a Remove step at the end of the timeline; a sketch, or a whole import in an imported model, is tombstoned by a delete step. Undo brings them back, and a tombstoned import or sketch also comes back with Restore ({key:edit.restore}) on its struck marker.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Restore
commands.summary: Brings back what a tombstone removed.
commands.details: Select a delete marker on the timeline first. The restore is a new step, so it can itself be undone.
commands.requires: Select a delete marker on the timeline first.

commands.title: Select what it touches
commands.summary: Selects the objects the current timeline step changed.
commands.details: Clicking a marker on the timeline already selects what the step made. Select what it touches ({key:edit.selecttouched}) then takes the whole bodies or components it changed, in the view and the browser.
commands.requires: Click a marker on the timeline first.

commands.title: Search commands
commands.summary: Finds any command by typing part of its name.
commands.details: Use the arrow keys and Enter to run the command. Every command of the menus and the ribbon is listed with its shortcut.

commands.title: Keyboard shortcuts
commands.summary: Shows every shortcut and lets you change them.
commands.details: Search by name or press the keys to find what they do. Conflicts are flagged before you save, and Restore default puts a command back to its default.

commands.title: Annotation author
commands.summary: Sets the name recorded on your notes and changes.
commands.details: The name appears on note cards and in the timeline's tooltips. It defaults to your system user name (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME or OPAD_AUTHOR when set).

commands.title: Undo history
commands.summary: Sets how many steps Undo keeps.
commands.details: The default is 50, the range 1 to 1000. Older steps stay in the document's history; only undo forgets them.

commands.title: Clear tessellation cache
commands.summary: Deletes OPAD's user cache: display meshes and the remembered copies of slow files.
commands.details: The cache makes large files open faster the second time. Clearing it frees disk space; the next open is slower once.

commands.title: Settings
commands.summary: Opens the settings menu: Preferences, keyboard shortcuts, the theme, the navigation preset and the panels.
commands.details: Everything that is set once lives in Preferences; this menu keeps the switches used every day. Every setting is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Preferences
commands.summary: Shows every setting of OPAD in one window, with a search.
commands.details: Pages for display, units and precision, sketch snaps, the grid, files, autosave, version control, keyboard and mouse, and AI access. Type in the search field to keep only the pages and rows that match. Changes apply at once and are kept for the next start.

commands.title: Help for this tool
commands.summary: Opens the guide of the tool you are using: what it does, its keys and its animated steps.
commands.details: With no tool running it opens the tool guide where you left it. Over a ribbon button or a menu entry, its key ({key:help.current}) expands that command's card instead.

commands.title: Tool guide
commands.summary: The commands, each with what it does, its current keys and, for most, an animated guide; searchable.
commands.details: Search by name or by what you want to do; pick a command to see its card and its clip, and click a step to loop it. A command not available now says what it needs.

commands.title: Shortcuts cheat sheet
commands.summary: Lists every keyboard shortcut and mouse gesture at a glance.
commands.details: The keys are grouped as in the command search, with the mouse of your navigation preset and the keys every tool knows. Search by name or key; Change shortcuts opens the editor, and Esc or the key that opened it ({key:help.shortcuts}) closes the sheet.

commands.title: Getting started
commands.summary: Six short animated lessons: move around, open, measure, sketch, make a solid and find any command.
commands.details: Each lesson shows its clip; all but the first have a Try it button that runs the command it teaches. The navigation lesson follows your mouse preset, and every key shown is your current one.

commands.title: Report a problem
commands.summary: Writes a problem report with what happened and the facts about OPAD and this computer.
commands.details: Nothing is sent by itself: copy the report or save it as a text file, or open the issue page and paste it there. The report names the document's kind and size, never its path or name.

commands.title: Third-party licences
commands.summary: Lists the libraries OPAD is built on, with their versions, sources and licence texts.
commands.details: OPAD itself is under the MIT licence; every library keeps its own. About Qt in the same window shows Qt's terms, and opad-cli licenses prints the same text.

commands.title: About Qt
commands.summary: Shows the version of Qt that OPAD runs on and Qt's licence.
commands.details: OPAD's windows, menus and panels are made with Qt, used under the LGPL version 3. The other libraries are listed under Third-party licences.

commands.title: About OPAD
commands.summary: Shows the OPAD version, its licence and the libraries it is built on.
commands.details: OPAD is free software under the MIT licence, built on Open CASCADE Technology, Qt and other libraries, each under its own licence. It has headless twins: opad-cli on the command line and the opad Python module. Both read and write the same documents.

commands.title: New sketch
commands.summary: Starts a sketch on an origin plane, a planar face or a construction plane.
commands.details: Pick an origin plane, a planar face, a construction plane or a sketch: the camera turns square to it. Place the origin or keep it and press OK; the ribbon switches to the Sketch tools. Finish sketch keeps the result as one step on the timeline.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Drawing to sketch
commands.summary: Turns an imported 2D drawing into an editable sketch in the drawing's own plane.
commands.details: Choose the layers to bring in; lines, arcs and circles become sketch curves you can constrain and extrude. The drawing itself stays as it was. Tick Construction only for helper layers such as centre lines. The curves come in unconstrained.
commands.requires: Open or create a document with an imported drawing (DXF, DWG or SVG) first.

commands.title: Parameters
commands.summary: Named values usable in any dimension or feature field.
commands.details: Define width = 40 mm once and type width, or an expression such as width / 2, wherever a value is asked. Changing a parameter regenerates everything that uses it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Regenerate
commands.summary: Recomputes every feature from the start of the timeline.
commands.details: Normally only what changed is recomputed. Use it after updating an imported file or to check that the whole history still builds.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Edit feature
commands.summary: Edits the feature or sketch selected on the timeline.
commands.details: The timeline rolls back to that step, so later steps are dimmed while you edit. OK regenerates everything after it.
commands.requires: Select a feature or a sketch on the timeline first, or double-click it.

commands.title: New component
commands.summary: Adds a component, named Component N, in the active component or the selected one.
commands.details: It becomes the active component, so what you make next goes into it (the Activate box under its name, or Activate new components, changes that), and its name is ready to type in the browser. Drag bodies onto it in the browser, or use Move to component.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Move to component
commands.summary: Moves the selection under another component, keeping it where it is.
commands.details: A list opens at the pointer with the document root and every component the selection can go to; type to narrow it, then click one or press Enter. What moves keeps its place in the world, as one step.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Component from selection
commands.summary: Puts the selected bodies and components into a new component, where they are.
commands.details: The new component is made in their nearest common component, in one step, and its name is ready to type in the browser. What moves into it keeps its place in the world.
commands.requires: Select bodies or components first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Activate new components
commands.summary: Makes each new component the active one as it is made.
commands.details: On, what you make after New component goes into it; off, the active component stays as it was. The Activate box under a new component's name changes this too.

commands.title: Activate component
commands.summary: Makes a component the active one: new sketches, features, bodies and imports go into it.
commands.details: Select a component, or a body in it, and run it; the radio button on a browser row does the same, and so does a double-click on a ghost. The rest of the model is ghosted, and the chip over the view names the active component: a click on it activates the document root again.
commands.requires: Select a component, or a body in it, that is not active yet.

commands.title: Activate root
commands.summary: Makes the document root active again, so nothing is ghosted.
commands.details: New sketches, features and bodies then go to the top of the document. A click on the active component's chip does the same.
commands.requires: Only while a component is active.

commands.title: Active component visibility
commands.summary: Chooses whether the rest of the model is ghosted while a component is active.
commands.details: On, everything outside the active component is drawn faintly and picked only as a reference; off, it is drawn and picked as it is. Inactive opacity, beside it in the Design menu and the chip's right-click menu, sets how faint the ghosts are.

commands.title: Only the active component's history
commands.summary: Keeps the timeline to the steps that touch the active component.
commands.details: Off, the other steps stay on the timeline, dimmed. It matters only while a component is active.

commands.title: Exploded view
commands.summary: Moves the parts of the assembly apart in the view, to show how it goes together.
commands.details: The Explode panel sets the level, the distance (a slider, with Play), the layout and what moves together; dashed lines show where each part belongs. Only the view changes, never the model, and Save exploded view keeps the arrangement as a named view.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Play explode
commands.summary: Moves the parts out, or back together when they are out.
commands.details: It animates the exploded view's distance. Space does the same in the Explode panel.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Collapse exploded view
commands.summary: Puts the parts back where the model has them.
commands.details: The exploded view's settings are kept, so Exploded view opens it again as it was. Saved exploded views do not change.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded.

commands.title: Save exploded view
commands.summary: Keeps the exploded arrangement as a named view in the document.
commands.details: Name it; choosing it later under View > Named views, or in the Explode panel, explodes the view again. A file open in viewer mode asks to become an OPAD document first.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Keep together
commands.summary: Makes the selected component move as one part in the exploded view, at any level.
commands.details: Use it for a subassembly that stays whole, such as a circuit board with its parts. The component's badge in the browser shows the rule, and a click on it switches the rule.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with a component selected.

commands.title: Explode its parts
commands.summary: Moves the selected component's parts apart in the exploded view, whatever the level.
commands.details: Use it for a folder of screws inside a part that is kept whole. Turn it off to let the component follow the level again.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with a component selected.

commands.title: Group (explode as one)
commands.summary: Makes the selected bodies and components move as one in the exploded view.
commands.details: The browser marks what moves together, and a saved exploded view keeps the group. Ungroup lets them move on their own again.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with two or more objects selected.

commands.title: Ungroup
commands.summary: Lets the selected objects of an explode group move on their own again.
commands.details: Only the exploded view changes. The browser stops marking them as moving together.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with a grouped object selected.

commands.title: Colour
commands.summary: Sets the colour of the selection.
commands.details: Pick the colour in the dialog; every selected object gets it, as one step. In viewer mode it is a view setting and is not saved.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Opacity
commands.summary: Makes the selection see-through, from 10 to 100 percent.
commands.details: A slider opens at the pointer (and in the right-click menu): the view follows it, and letting go keeps it as one step. Lower opacity lets you see parts inside a housing; picking still works on see-through bodies.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Lock
commands.summary: Locks the selection against picking and edits, or unlocks it.
commands.details: Locked objects stay visible but the hover no longer finds them, so you can work on what is in front or around. Use it again to unlock.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Box
commands.summary: A box on a plane at a position, sized by length, width and height.
commands.details: Length runs along the plane's X, width along its Y and height along its normal; a negative height grows the other way. It is centred on the position in X and Y unless you turn that off. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Cylinder
commands.summary: A cylinder standing on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Its axis is the plane's normal; set the diameter and the height. A negative height grows the other way. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Sphere
commands.summary: A sphere centred on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Set the diameter; the centre is the position on the plane. Combine it with other bodies to round off shapes. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Cone
commands.summary: A cone or a truncated cone standing on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Set the base and top diameters and the height; a top diameter above zero cuts the tip off. Its axis is the plane's normal. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Torus
commands.summary: A ring centred on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Set the ring diameter, through the middle of the tube, and the section diameter of the tube. Useful for O-rings and handles. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Extrude
commands.summary: Pulls sketch profiles or planar faces along their normal into a solid.
commands.details: Pick the profiles, then drag the arrow or type the distance. Symmetric splits the distance on both sides, and the extent can also run through all or up to a face or body. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Revolve
commands.summary: Turns sketch profiles about an axis into a solid.
commands.details: Pick the profiles, then the axis: a sketch line, an edge or an origin axis. A full turn is 360 degrees; Symmetric splits the angle on both sides. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Sweep
commands.summary: Moves a profile along a path into a solid.
commands.details: Pick one profile, then the path: sketch curves or edges. Keep the profile at the start of the path and smaller than its tightest bend. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Loft
commands.summary: Blends through two or more profiles, in the order they are picked.
commands.details: Pick the profiles one after another, usually on parallel planes. Straight sides makes ruled faces between them instead of a smooth skin. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Pipe
commands.summary: A round section along a path.
commands.details: Pick the path and set the diameter; Hollow adds a wall thickness. Good for cables, tubing and handrails. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Coil
commands.summary: A round or square section wound about an axis: springs and threads.
commands.details: Set the coil diameter, the pitch between turns and the number of turns. Left-handed winds it the other way. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Thicken
commands.summary: Gives faces a thickness: a solid skin over the picked faces.
commands.details: Pick the faces and set the thickness; Other side grows it inward. Useful to turn a surface into a part. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Hole
commands.summary: Drills holes at sketch points, into the material behind the sketch.
commands.details: Pick the sketch points, then choose a simple, counterbored or countersunk hole with its diameter and depth. Each point gets one hole.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Fillet
commands.summary: Rounds edges.
commands.details: Pick the edges and set the radius; edges that meet tangentially are rounded together. By rule… in the panel, or Select similar, picks every similar edge at once.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Chamfer
commands.summary: Bevels edges.
commands.details: Pick the edges and set one distance, or two distances for an unequal bevel. Chamfers break sharp edges and ease assembly.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Shell
commands.summary: Hollows a body; the picked faces are removed and become openings.
commands.details: Pick the faces to open and set the wall thickness. To hollow it closed, click Bodies to hollow in the panel and pick the body.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Draft
commands.summary: Tilts faces about a neutral plane, for moulds.
commands.details: Pick the faces, the neutral plane and the angle. A few degrees of draft lets a part come out of its mould.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Press pull
commands.summary: Pushes planar faces in or pulls them out.
commands.details: Pick one or more faces and drag the arrow or type the distance; a negative value pushes into the material. The face moves straight along its normal: sides square to it extend, slanted sides do not (use Draft for those).
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Remove faces
commands.summary: Deletes faces and closes the gap by extending the faces around them.
commands.details: Pick the faces of a hole, fillet, chamfer or boss and press Enter; the neighbouring faces grow until they meet. Imported bodies can be simplified this way. It is also on Press pull's menu and on the right-click menu of a picked face.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Scale
commands.summary: Resizes bodies uniformly.
commands.details: Set the factor: 2 doubles, 0.5 halves. Scale about the origin or about each body's centre of mass.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Combine
commands.summary: Joins, cuts or intersects bodies.
commands.details: Pick the target bodies, then the tool bodies, and choose the operation. Keep tools leaves the tool bodies in place after the cut.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Split body
commands.summary: Cuts bodies in two along a plane.
commands.details: Pick the bodies and the splitting plane. Each body becomes two bodies in place, which you can then move, hide or delete.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Mirror
commands.summary: Makes mirrored copies of bodies about a plane.
commands.details: Pick the bodies and the mirror plane. Model half of a symmetric part and mirror the rest. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Rectangular pattern
commands.summary: Copies bodies in rows and columns.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, a direction, the count and the spacing; turn on a second direction for a grid. Changing the count later updates every copy. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Circular pattern
commands.summary: Copies bodies about an axis.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, the axis, the count and the total angle. 360 degrees spreads the copies evenly around a full turn. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Move / copy
commands.summary: Moves or copies bodies by distances and an optional turn.
commands.details: Pick the bodies and type X, Y and Z; turn on Rotate for an axis and an angle. Make a copy leaves the original in place, and every value can be an expression.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Remove
commands.summary: Takes bodies out of the design from this point on.
commands.details: The history keeps them: roll the timeline back before this step and they are there. Use it for tool bodies that are no longer needed.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Construction plane
commands.summary: A plane to sketch on, or to mirror, split and draft about.
commands.details: Make it offset from a plane, at an angle about an axis, midway between two planes, through three points or through a point normal to an axis. It follows its references when they change.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Construction axis
commands.summary: An axis to revolve or pattern about.
commands.details: Make it along an edge or through a round face's centre, through two points, or normal to a plane through a point. Revolve and the circular pattern can pick it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Interference check
commands.summary: Records an interference check in the history that runs again whenever its bodies change.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, or none for all solids, and an optional clearance. With Fail on set, a finding marks the step as an error on the timeline.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Finish sketch
commands.summary: Ends the sketch and keeps it.
commands.details: The sketch becomes one step on the timeline and its closed regions turn into profiles for Extrude and Revolve. The camera and the ribbon return to where you were.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Cancel sketch
commands.summary: Leaves the sketch and discards the changes made since it opened.
commands.details: A new sketch is not created at all; an edited sketch goes back to how it was. Use Finish sketch to keep your work. If you changed the sketch, you confirm discarding first.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Sketch tools
commands.summary: Opens the sketch tool panel: the tool's steps and fields, precise input, constraints and snaps.
commands.details: Type exact coordinates there, absolute, relative or as length and angle, to place points. The other pages list the constraints and set the snaps and solver.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Command line
commands.summary: A line at the bottom left of the sketch for drafting by the keyboard: type a tool's name or a value.
commands.details: A word runs a tool or an editing command (its name or a short form such as LINE or REC); anything else goes into the step's value boxes, then Enter. Up and Down recall earlier entries, and its close button hides it until this command ({key:sketch.commandLine}) opens it again.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Redefine sketch plane
commands.summary: Moves the sketch to another plane, keeping its geometry.
commands.details: Pick a new origin plane, planar face or construction plane, place the sketch origin on it and press OK. Features built on the sketch follow it to the new place.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Spline node weights
commands.summary: Edits the weights of a spline node and its handles.
commands.details: Select a node of a spline (or double-click it), set the weights and press Enter or Apply. A heavier node pulls the curve closer to it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Find open ends
commands.summary: Marks endpoints that meet nothing, which is why a profile is not closed.
commands.details: Each open end gets a red ring. Close the gaps by dragging the ends together or with Heal endpoints.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Construction
commands.summary: Turns the selected curves into construction geometry, or back.
commands.details: Construction curves are dashed: they guide and constrain but never form profiles. Use them for centre lines and helper circles.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Copy with base point
commands.summary: Copies the selected sketch curves about a point you click.
commands.details: Select the curves, run it and click the base point; a paste then carries the copy on the pointer by that point. The constraints among the curves come along.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open, with curves selected.

commands.title: Show or hide constraints
commands.summary: Shows or hides the constraint badges in the sketch.
commands.details: Hiding them only declutters the view: the constraints keep holding. Constraints in conflict and selected ones still show.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Select
commands.summary: Selects, drags and edits sketch geometry; double-click a dimension to change it.
commands.details: Dragging moves geometry while the constraints keep holding. Del deletes the selection and Construction ({key:sketch.construction}) makes it construction geometry.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Line
commands.summary: Draws connected lines; click point after point.
commands.details: Each click ends one segment and starts the next. Close the loop on the start point, or press Enter or double-click to stop; horizontal and vertical constraints are added as you draw.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Rectangle
commands.summary: Draws a rectangle from two opposite corners.
commands.details: Click the first corner, then the opposite one. Its sides get horizontal and vertical constraints, ready to dimension.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Centre rectangle
commands.summary: Draws a rectangle from its centre and a corner.
commands.details: Click the centre, then a corner; the rectangle grows symmetrically. Handy for parts centred on the origin.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 3-point rectangle
commands.summary: Draws a rotated rectangle: a corner, the base direction, then the height.
commands.details: The first two clicks set one side at any angle. The third sets how far the opposite side lies.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle from its centre and a point on it.
commands.details: Click the centre, then click again to set the size. Dimension the diameter afterwards to fix it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 2-point circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle across a diameter: two opposite points.
commands.details: Click one end of the diameter, then the other. Useful when the circle must touch two existing points.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 3-point circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle through three points.
commands.details: Click three points on the circle, in any order. Snap to existing points to fit a circle through them.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Tangent circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle tangent to two lines with a set radius.
commands.details: Set the radius, pick the two lines, then click on the side where the circle should sit. It stays tangent when the lines move.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 3-point arc
commands.summary: Draws an arc through a start, an end and a point on it.
commands.details: Click the start, the end, then move to bend the arc and click. The third click sets how far it bulges.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Centre arc
commands.summary: Draws an arc from its centre, a start and an end.
commands.details: Click the centre, then the start, which sets the radius, then sweep to the end and click. A radius dimension fixes its size afterwards.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Tangent arc
commands.summary: Draws an arc that continues tangentially from the end of a line.
commands.details: Pick the line's endpoint, then click where the arc ends. The joint stays smooth when you edit either curve.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Ellipse
commands.summary: Draws an ellipse: centre, end of the first axis, then the second axis.
commands.details: The first axis can lie at any angle. The third click sets the half-width across it.
